scope: All 92 active and 347 ignored Codacy repository/main records; fresh per-occurrence semantic review, not approval inherited from historical ignored status.
method: Retrieve complete paginated active/ignored/configuration/file inventory and exact-revision logs.
Locate each provider statement in exact baseline Git blob bytes without exporting source-line contents.
Inspect every matched occurrence, enclosing scope, controlling validation/fixture root and relevant callers; historical comments are leads only.
Check numeric literal exactness independently through AST/runtime integer conversion.
Record superseded statements and provider failures separately; neither is approved as a present false positive.
Keep remote decisions unapplied until final source changes are semantically renewed.

entries.rationale: This provider occurrence still names standard-library version 1.26.0, while the exact baseline go.mod declares 1.26.6 and Codacy file metrics report zero issues for this file. Both initial and fresh UI-triggered analysis logs fail Trivy with Line numbers not supported. This is unresolved provider analysis state, not a renewed false-positive or a clean vulnerability scan.

Each fetch is inside the private HTTP test suite. runTests creates an isolated temporary database/configuration, clears WEB_HOST, starts the actual server on an ephemeral port, awaits listening, asserts its native address is loopback and constructs baseUrl from that numeric port. Every inspected helper receives that base unchanged. Route constants, fixture identifiers and query strings alter only the path/body. Mutation callbacks are fixture implementations. The individual occurrence records below identify its exact enclosing helper and destination expression.
entries.limitation: Applies to the inspected checkout and caller authority; source or caller changes require renewed semantic review.

All flagged filesystem operations are in private test helpers called from runTests with a freshly created temporary root and fixed database/state/backup children. Closed test cases intentionally create malformed archives or symlinks in that owned tree and assert rejection. Scheduler paths are fixed leaf names under the same fixture root; no request path reaches a filesystem operation. Awaited backup rejection and timer behavior are deliberately exercised and must remain native.
entries.limitation: Does not claim immunity to a hostile concurrent actor with the same operating-system account. Negative traversal fixture strings are intentional test input, not production paths.

finalSemanticDeltaReview.tests/test_backup.js: Composite required-table assertion split into two independent asserts for fallback runs/candidates. Both requirements remain mandatory before database initialization; fixed disposable path fixtures and cleanup authority unchanged. No weakening or broadening of filesystem inputs.
